newsitem.title: INDIA: India rupee ends at 35.88/89 vs dlr in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: India rupee ends at 35.88/89 vs dlr in quiet trade.

text.p: The Indian rupee ended at 35.88/89 against the dollar on Tuesday, little changed from the opening level of 35.89/90, dealers said.
Dealers said the rupee moved in a narrow band on Tuesday.
"The highest business was done at 35.9125 (rupees to a dollar) and the lowest at 35.8850," a dealer said.
One bank dealer lamented that the market was active only when a leading player entered the scene and was "dead" in its absence. The gainer in this situation was the rupee, he said.

He was referring to the rupee swinging to 35.90 level in recent weeks on dollar purchases by a leading Calcutta bank. This bank has been abstaining this week, leading to tranquility on the exchange front.
"The rupee is doing a bit of a yoyo but the trend appears downwards," said a dealer at a foreign bank. He said 35.84 looked like the bottom and 35.94/95 the upper limit.
"The test on the upside would obviously be a more serious one," the dealer said. But many dealers do not expect the rupee to breach the 36 per dollar barrier until mid-February.
Premia opened higher and kept edging up in the forward dollar market but fell towards the close, dealers said.
The six-month annualised premia closed at 6.96 percent, marginally lower than Monday's closing level of 6.74 percent.
